subproblems.title: Compatible compactly supported pull-backs exist (cut-off of Simon 2.23)
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P Q j : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)) (V : Set (Eucl Q)) (A : Set (Eucl P)) (f : Eucl P → Eucl Q), IsOpen U → A ⊆ U → ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) f → (∀ K : Set (Eucl Q), IsCompact K → K ⊆ V → IsCompact (f ⁻¹' K ∩ A)) → ∀ ω : TestFormOn V j, ∃ (η : TestFormOn U j) (ζ : Eucl P → ℝ) (N : Set (Eucl P)), IsOpen N ∧ A ⊆ N ∧ (∀ x, 0 ≤ ζ x ∧ ζ x ≤ 1) ∧ (∀ x, (η : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) j) x = ζ x • ((ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl Q) j) (f x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ f x)) ∧ (∀ x ∈ N, (η : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) j) x = ((ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl Q) j) (f x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ f x)) ∧ tsupport (η : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) j) ⊆ f ⁻¹' tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl Q) j)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reused comparator-accepted declaration: this child is DAG node root.integrality_weak_limits-a1.smooth_pushforward-a1.compatible_form-a1 (status accepted, candidate commit fd5f1e29719e3bfa62df774678e3c6879599f8f9, isolated comparator passed = True, declaration Submission.iwl_sp_exists_compatible_testForm). It is reused by name with the byte-identical frozen Lean type, title and statement, so no new DAG node is created and it has no sibling prerequisites in this decomposition. It is already a resolved dependency of the selected parent root.deformation-a1.onto_skeleton-a1.pushforward_homotopy-a1.lipschitz_pushforward-a1.existence-a1 (dph_lpf_existence). Role in this decomposition: the 'reused compatible_form' of step 3 of the supplied proof. It is consumed by the new sibling bounded_compatible (its step 1, with P := m, Q := m′, j := k, U := O, V := univ, the set A and the map f), which in turn supplies the parent's forms η_n(ω) for n ≥ n₀ (with f := G_n, A := spt X, O := (spt X)_{r/2}). The accepted, independently audited natural-language proof of this exact statement follows verbatim.

Source: fact (F5) of the parent proof (the cut-off function ζ of Simon 2.23, p. 139), filled in. It is stated for an arbitrary set A ⊆ U on which f is proper; the parent uses A = spt X. Neither MapsTo nor openness of V is needed.

Notation: p(x) := Df(x)^#(ω(f(x))) = (ω(f x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ f x) is the pull-back form f^#ω. C^∞ means smoothness of order ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞), i.e. of every finite order.

1. (The compact set.) ω ∈ D^j(V) has compact support, so tsupport ω is compact (HasCompactSupport.isCompact), and tsupport ω ⊆ V. By the properness hypothesis, K := f⁻¹(tsupport ω) ∩ A is compact, and K ⊆ A ⊆ U.
2. (Thickenings.) K is compact, U is open and K ⊆ U, so there is δ₀ > 0 with cthickening δ₀ K ⊆ U (IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open). Define:
   - O := thickening (δ₀/2) K, open, with K ⊆ O (self_subset_thickening, as δ₀/2 > 0);
   - C := cthickening (δ₀/2) K, closed, with O ⊆ C (thickening_subset_cthickening);
   - s := thickening δ₀ K, open, with C ⊆ s (cthickening_subset_thickening', since 0 < δ₀ and δ₀/2 < δ₀).
   If K = ∅, all these sets are empty and the argument below still applies.
3. (The cut-off.) Smooth Urysohn (exists_contDiff_support_eq_eq_one_iff with n = ⊤, applied to the open set s and the closed set C ⊆ s) gives a C^∞ function ζ : ℝ^P → ℝ with range ζ ⊆ [0, 1], support ζ = s, and ζ(x) = 1 ⟺ x ∈ C. Consequently:
   - 0 ≤ ζ ≤ 1 everywhere, and ζ = 1 on O;
   - tsupport ζ = closure s ⊆ cthickening δ₀ K ⊆ U (closure_thickening_subset_cthickening);
   - cthickening δ₀ K is compact (IsCompact.cthickening; ℝ^P is proper), so its closed subset tsupport ζ is compact, i.e. ζ has compact support.
4. (p is C^∞.)
   - x ↦ Df(x) is C^∞ because f is C^∞ (ContDiff.fderiv_right, using ∞ + 1 ≤ ∞).
   - x ↦ ω(f(x)) is C^∞ as the composition of the C^∞ maps ω (a test form) and f.
   - B ↦ compContinuousLinearMapCLM B is C^∞. It sends a continuous linear map B : ℝ^P → ℝ^Q to the continuous linear map α ↦ α.compContinuousLinearMap B on j-covectors, and it is analytic on the whole space (ContinuousAlternatingMap.analyticOnNhd_compContinuousLinearMapCLM), hence C^∞ (AnalyticOnNhd.contDiff).
   - Since p(x) = (compContinuousLinearMapCLM (Df(x)))(ω(f(x))), p is C^∞ (ContDiff.comp, ContDiff.clm_apply).
5. (The test form.) Define η(x) := ζ(x)·p(x). η is C^∞ (ContDiff.smul). Also tsupport η ⊆ tsupport ζ (tsupport_smul_subset_left), so η has compact support (HasCompactSupport.smul_right) and tsupport η ⊆ U by step 3. Hence η ∈ D^j(U) = TestFormOn U j, and η(x) = ζ(x)·p(x) for all x by definition.
6. (Support.) If f(x) ∉ tsupport ω, then ω(f(x)) = 0 (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport). Hence p(x) = 0, the pull-back of the zero covector being zero, and η(x) = 0. So support η ⊆ f⁻¹(tsupport ω). This set is closed, since f is continuous and tsupport ω is closed, so tsupport η ⊆ f⁻¹(tsupport ω) (closure_minimal).
7. (The open set.) Put N := O ∪ f⁻¹(ℝ^Q ∖ tsupport ω), an open set. A ⊆ N: for x ∈ A, if f(x) ∈ tsupport ω then x ∈ K ⊆ O; otherwise x ∈ f⁻¹(ℝ^Q ∖ tsupport ω).
8. (η = p on N.) If x ∈ O ⊆ C, then ζ(x) = 1 and η(x) = p(x). If f(x) ∉ tsupport ω, then p(x) = 0 = η(x) by step 6.
9. Steps 3, 5, 6, 7 and 8 show that η, ζ and N have all the required properties. ∎
proof_key_steps: Properness makes K := f⁻¹(tsupport ω) ∩ A a compact subset of the open set U.
Smooth Urysohn on thickenings of K gives a C^∞ cut-off ζ with values in [0, 1], compact support in U and ζ = 1 on a neighbourhood O of K.
The pull-back p = f^#ω is C^∞ (B ↦ B^# is analytic), so η := ζ·p ∈ D^j(U) with tsupport η ⊆ f⁻¹(tsupport ω).
η = p on the open set N := O ∪ f⁻¹(ℝ^Q ∖ tsupport ω), which contains A.

subproblems.title: Pull-back of covectors: |L^#α| ≤ ‖L‖^j |α| for the Euclidean coefficient norm
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P Q j : ℕ) (L : Eucl P →L[ℝ] Eucl Q) (α : Covector (Eucl Q) j), covectorEuclideanNorm (α.compContinuousLinearMap L) ≤ ‖L‖ ^ j * covectorEuclideanNorm α
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reused comparator-accepted declaration: this child is DAG node root.integrality_weak_limits-a1.smooth_pushforward-a1.pullback_norm-a1 (status accepted, candidate commit 3e52d3e816fb507ab732d7ad15590fb7280bc981, isolated comparator passed = True, declaration Submission.iwl_sp_covectorEuclideanNorm_pullback_le). It is reused by name with the byte-identical frozen Lean type, title and statement, so no new DAG node is created and it has no sibling prerequisites in this decomposition. It is already a resolved dependency of the selected parent root.deformation-a1.onto_skeleton-a1.pushforward_homotopy-a1.lipschitz_pushforward-a1.existence-a1 (dph_lpf_existence). Role in this decomposition: the 'reused pullback_norm' of step 3 of the supplied proof. It is consumed by the new sibling bounded_compatible (its step 4(a), with P := m, Q := m′, j := k, L := fderiv ℝ f x, α := ω(f x)) for the pointwise bound |ω(f x)∘Df(x)| ≤ ‖Df(x)‖^k·|ω(f x)|, which yields |η_n(ω)| ≤ Λ^k·C and hence the mass bound Λ^k·M(X) of the parent. The accepted, independently audited natural-language proof of this exact statement follows verbatim.

Source: fact (F3) of the parent proof. The parent justifies (F3) by the singular value decomposition. Transferring that argument to covectorEuclideanNorm, which is defined on continuous alternating maps through the standard basis, would need an SVD factorization L = Σ_i σ_i u_i ⊗ v_i and the orthonormality, for this norm, of the wedges of an arbitrary orthonormal basis. The pinned Mathlib has singular values (LinearMap.singularValues) and an inner product on the abstract exterior power ⋀[ℝ]^n E, but neither the factorization nor any link to covectorEuclideanNorm. The same inequality is therefore proved by the elementary tensor (Hilbert–Schmidt) argument below, which uses only the standard bases.

Notation:
- e_1, …, e_P and e′_1, …, e′_Q are the standard orthonormal bases of ℝ^P and ℝ^Q (EuclideanSpace.basisFun);
- for i : Fin j → Fin P, e∘i := (e_{i(1)}, …, e_{i(j)}), and similarly e′∘i for i : Fin j → Fin Q;
- |γ| := covectorEuclideanNorm γ, so for a j-covector γ on ℝ^m (m ∈ {P, Q}, with the corresponding standard basis), |γ|² = Σ_{I : Fin j → Fin m strictly increasing} γ(e∘I)²;
- L^#α := α.compContinuousLinearMap L, so (L^#α)(v₁, …, v_j) = α(Lv₁, …, Lv_j);
- |·| on vectors is the Euclidean norm, ⟨·,·⟩ the inner product, and ‖L‖ the operator norm.

1. (Sum over all index tuples.) For every j-covector γ on ℝ^m: Σ_{i : Fin j → Fin m} γ(e∘i)² = j!·|γ|².
   (a) If i is not injective, e∘i has two equal entries, so γ(e∘i) = 0 because γ is alternating.
   (b) The map (I, σ) ↦ I ∘ σ is a bijection from pairs (I strictly increasing Fin j → Fin m, σ a permutation of Fin j) onto the injective maps Fin j → Fin m.
      - Surjectivity: for injective i, the tuple i ∘ (sort i) is monotone (Tuple.monotone_sort) and injective, hence strictly increasing. With I := i ∘ sort i and σ := (sort i)⁻¹, I ∘ σ = i.
      - Injectivity: if I ∘ σ = I′ ∘ σ′, then range I = range I′. A strictly increasing map Fin j → Fin m is determined by its range (it enumerates the range in increasing order), so I = I′, and then σ = σ′ because I is injective.
   (c) For such pairs, γ(e∘(I ∘ σ)) = sign(σ)·γ(e∘I) (AlternatingMap.map_perm), so γ(e∘(I ∘ σ))² = γ(e∘I)².
   By (a)–(c), Σ_i γ(e∘i)² = Σ_{I strictly increasing} Σ_σ γ(e∘I)² = j!·Σ_I γ(e∘I)² = j!·|γ|², because Fin j has j! permutations.
2. (One slot.) For every linear functional λ : ℝ^Q → ℝ: Σ_{a=1}^{P} λ(Le_a)² ≤ ‖L‖²·Σ_{b=1}^{Q} λ(e′_b)².
   - Put g := Σ_b λ(e′_b)e′_b ∈ ℝ^Q. Then λ(y) = ⟨g, y⟩ for every y (expand y = Σ_b ⟨e′_b, y⟩e′_b), and |g|² = Σ_b λ(e′_b)².
   - Put u := Σ_a λ(Le_a)e_a ∈ ℝ^P. Then |u|² = Σ_a λ(Le_a)², and by linearity λ(Lu) = Σ_a λ(Le_a)² = |u|².
   - By Cauchy–Schwarz, |u|² = ⟨g, Lu⟩ ≤ |g|·|Lu| ≤ |g|·‖L‖·|u|.
   Hence |u| ≤ ‖L‖·|g| (trivial if u = 0, otherwise divide by |u|), and squaring gives the claim.
3. (All slots, by induction on j.) For every j ∈ ℕ and every j-multilinear map β : (ℝ^Q)^j → ℝ:
   Σ_{i : Fin j → Fin P} β(Le_{i(1)}, …, Le_{i(j)})² ≤ ‖L‖^{2j}·Σ_{i : Fin j → Fin Q} β(e′∘i)².
   For j = 0 both sides equal β()², because there is exactly one empty tuple and ‖L‖⁰ = 1.
   For the step j → j + 1, write tuples as i = Fin.cons a i′ with a ∈ Fin P and i′ : Fin j → Fin P (and likewise over Fin Q). Write Le∘i′ := (Le_{i′(1)}, …, Le_{i′(j)}).
   - For fixed a, the induction hypothesis applied to the j-multilinear map β(Le_a, ·) gives Σ_{i′} β(Le_a, Le∘i′)² ≤ ‖L‖^{2j}·Σ_{i″ : Fin j → Fin Q} β(Le_a, e′∘i″)².
   - Summing over a, the left sides add up to Σ_{i : Fin (j+1) → Fin P} β(Le_{i(1)}, …, Le_{i(j+1)})². After exchanging the finite sums, the right sides add up to ‖L‖^{2j}·Σ_{i″} Σ_a λ_{i″}(Le_a)², where λ_{i″}(y) := β(y, e′∘i″) is a linear functional on ℝ^Q.
   - By step 2, this is at most ‖L‖^{2j}·Σ_{i″} ‖L‖²·Σ_b β(e′_b, e′∘i″)² = ‖L‖^{2(j+1)}·Σ_{i : Fin (j+1) → Fin Q} β(e′∘i)².
   This proves the claim for j + 1.
4. (Conclusion.) Apply step 3 to β := α, an alternating and in particular multilinear map. Since (L^#α)(e∘i) = α(Le_{i(1)}, …, Le_{i(j)}), this gives
   Σ_{i : Fin j → Fin P} (L^#α)(e∘i)² ≤ ‖L‖^{2j}·Σ_{i : Fin j → Fin Q} α(e′∘i)².
   By step 1, applied to L^#α on ℝ^P and to α on ℝ^Q, this reads j!·|L^#α|² ≤ ‖L‖^{2j}·j!·|α|². Dividing by j! > 0 gives |L^#α|² ≤ (‖L‖^j·|α|)². Both |L^#α| and ‖L‖^j·|α| are nonnegative, so |L^#α| ≤ ‖L‖^j·|α|.
   No restriction on j, P, Q is used. For j = 0 both sides equal |α()|; if j > P or j > Q, the corresponding sums over strictly increasing indices are empty. ∎
proof_key_steps: For an alternating γ, the sum of γ(e∘i)² over all index tuples equals j!·|γ|²: non-injective tuples give 0, and injective ones are uniquely permutations of increasing ones.
Single-slot bound Σ_a λ(L e_a)² ≤ ‖L‖² Σ_b λ(e′_b)², via the Riesz vector g of λ, u = Σ_a λ(Le_a)e_a and Cauchy–Schwarz.
Induction over the j slots of a multilinear map gives Σ_i α(L e∘i)² ≤ ‖L‖^{2j} Σ_i α(e′∘i)².
Divide by j! and take square roots: |L^#α| ≤ ‖L‖^j |α|.

subproblems.title: Bounded compatible pull-back forms for a C^∞ map that is proper on A and has ‖Df‖ ≤ Λ on an open O ⊇ A (supplied Steps 2–3)
subproblems.statement: Notation: ℝ^p := Eucl p; D^q(ℝ^p) := TestFormOn univ q; |γ| := covectorEuclideanNorm γ; for a covector γ on ℝ^{m′} and a continuous linear map T : ℝ^m → ℝ^{m′}, γ∘T := γ.compContinuousLinearMap T; C^∞ means ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞). Let m, m′, k ∈ ℕ, let f : ℝ^m → ℝ^{m′} be C^∞, let A ⊆ O ⊆ ℝ^m with O open, and let Λ ∈ ℝ≥0 with ‖fderiv ℝ f x‖ ≤ Λ for every x ∈ O. Assume that f is proper on A: f⁻¹(K) ∩ A is compact for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^{m′}. Then for every ω ∈ D^k(ℝ^{m′}) there is η ∈ D^k(ℝ^m) such that (i) η is compatible with (f, ω) near A: there is an open N ⊆ ℝ^m with A ⊆ N and η(x) = ω(f(x))∘(fderiv ℝ f x) for every x ∈ N; and (ii) for every C ∈ ℝ with |ω(y)| ≤ C for all y ∈ ℝ^{m′}, one has |η(x)| ≤ Λ^k·C for all x ∈ ℝ^m.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (m m' k : ℕ) (f : Eucl m → Eucl m') (A O : Set (Eucl m)) (Λ : ℝ≥0), IsOpen O → A ⊆ O → ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) f → (∀ x ∈ O, ‖fderiv ℝ f x‖ ≤ Λ) → (∀ K : Set (Eucl m'), IsCompact K → IsCompact (f ⁻¹' K ∩ A)) → ∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Eucl m')) k, ∃ η : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Eucl m)) k, (∃ N : Set (Eucl m), IsOpen N ∧ A ⊆ N ∧ ∀ x ∈ N, (η : DifferentialForm (Eucl m) k) x = ((ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl m') k) (f x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ f x)) ∧ ∀ C : ℝ, (∀ y, covectorEuclideanNorm ((ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl m') k) y) ≤ C) → ∀ x, covectorEuclideanNorm ((η : DifferentialForm (Eucl m) k) x) ≤ (Λ : ℝ) ^ k * C
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Steps 2 and 3 of the parent proof (homogeneity of |·|; compatible forms with bounds), stated for one C^∞ map f that is proper on a set A and has ‖Df‖ ≤ Λ on an open O ⊇ A. The parent applies it for n ≥ n₀ with f := G_n, A := spt X and O := O₀ = (spt X)_{r/2}, and puts η_n(ω) := 0 for n < n₀. Notation as in the statement; Df(x) := fderiv ℝ f x. Recall that TestFormOn U k consists of the differential k-forms that are C^∞, have compact support, and satisfy tsupport ⊆ U.

1. (Compatible form; reused compatible_form.) Apply iwl_sp_exists_compatible_testForm with P := m, Q := m′, j := k, U := O, V := univ, the set A and the map f. Its hypotheses hold: O is open, A ⊆ O, f is C^∞, and for every compact K ⊆ univ the set f⁻¹(K) ∩ A is compact by the properness hypothesis. Applied to ω ∈ TestFormOn univ k, it gives η₀ ∈ TestFormOn O k, ζ : ℝ^m → ℝ and N ⊆ ℝ^m such that N is open, A ⊆ N, 0 ≤ ζ(x) ≤ 1 for all x, η₀(x) = ζ(x)·(ω(f x)∘Df(x)) for all x, and η₀(x) = ω(f x)∘Df(x) for all x ∈ N. Its last conclusion (tsupport η₀ ⊆ f⁻¹(tsupport ω)) is not needed.
2. (Change of domain.) η₀ is C^∞ and has compact support because η₀ ∈ TestFormOn O k, and tsupport η₀ ⊆ univ holds trivially. So the same differential form is an element η of TestFormOn univ k = D^k(ℝ^m), with η(x) = η₀(x) for every x. By step 1, η(x) = ω(f x)∘Df(x) for every x ∈ N, where N is open and A ⊆ N. This is (i).
3. (Homogeneity of |·|.) For c ∈ ℝ and a k-covector γ on ℝ^m: |c·γ| = |c|·|γ|. By definition |γ| = √Σ_I [I strictly increasing] γ(e_{I(1)}, …, e_{I(k)})², summed over I : Fin k → Fin m, where e is the standard basis. Since (c·γ)(v) = c·γ(v), every term of the sum for c·γ is c² times the corresponding term for γ, so that sum equals c²·Σ (Finset.mul_sum). Hence |c·γ| = √(c²·Σ) = √(c²)·√Σ = |c|·|γ| (Real.sqrt_mul with c² ≥ 0, Real.sqrt_sq_eq_abs).
4. (Bound.) Let C ∈ ℝ with |ω(y)| ≤ C for all y. Then C ≥ |ω(0)| ≥ 0 (covectorEuclideanNorm_nonneg), so Λ^k·C ≥ 0. Fix x ∈ ℝ^m.
   (a) Case x ∈ O. By steps 1–3 and ζ(x) ≥ 0: |η(x)| = |ζ(x)·(ω(f x)∘Df(x))| = ζ(x)·|ω(f x)∘Df(x)|. Since ζ(x) ≤ 1 and |·| ≥ 0, this is at most |ω(f x)∘Df(x)|. The reused pullback_norm (iwl_sp_covectorEuclideanNorm_pullback_le with P := m, Q := m′, j := k, L := Df(x), α := ω(f x)) gives |ω(f x)∘Df(x)| ≤ ‖Df(x)‖^k·|ω(f x)|. By hypothesis 0 ≤ ‖Df(x)‖ ≤ Λ, because x ∈ O, so ‖Df(x)‖^k ≤ Λ^k (u ↦ u^k is monotone on [0, ∞); pow_le_pow_left₀). Together with 0 ≤ |ω(f x)| ≤ C and Λ^k ≥ 0 this gives ‖Df(x)‖^k·|ω(f x)| ≤ Λ^k·C. Hence |η(x)| ≤ Λ^k·C.
   (b) Case x ∉ O. Since η₀ ∈ TestFormOn O k, tsupport η₀ ⊆ O, so x ∉ tsupport η₀. Hence η(x) = η₀(x) = 0 (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport) and |η(x)| = |0| = 0 ≤ Λ^k·C (covectorEuclideanNorm_zero).
   This proves (ii) for every x.
5. (Conclusion.) η ∈ D^k(ℝ^m) satisfies (i) by step 2 and (ii) by step 4. ∎
proof_key_steps: Write f^#ω for the pull-back x ↦ ω(f x)∘Df(x). compatible_form with U := O and V := univ gives η₀ ∈ D^k(O), ζ with values in [0, 1], and an open N ⊇ A such that η₀ = ζ·f^#ω everywhere and η₀ = f^#ω on N.
tsupport η₀ ⊆ O ⊆ univ, so η₀ is an element η of D^k(ℝ^m), compatible with (f, ω) on N.
|c·γ| = |c|·|γ| for the coefficient norm, because the sum of squares scales by c².
On O: |η(x)| = ζ(x)|f^#ω(x)| ≤ ‖Df(x)‖^k|ω(f x)| ≤ Λ^k·C by pullback_norm. Off O: η(x) = 0 because tsupport η₀ ⊆ O.

subproblems.title: A real sequence converges if a(q(i)) − a(p(i)) → 0 for all pairs of index maps p, q → ∞ (real-analysis part of supplied Step 6)
subproblems.statement: Let a : ℕ → ℝ. Assume that for all maps p, q : ℕ → ℕ with p(i) → ∞ and q(i) → ∞ as i → ∞ (Tendsto p atTop atTop and Tendsto q atTop atTop), a(q(i)) − a(p(i)) → 0 as i → ∞. Then a converges: there is s ∈ ℝ with a(n) → s as n → ∞.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ a : ℕ → ℝ, (∀ p q : ℕ → ℕ, Tendsto p atTop atTop → Tendsto q atTop atTop → Tendsto (fun i => a (q i) - a (p i)) atTop (𝓝 0)) → ∃ s : ℝ, Tendsto a atTop (𝓝 s)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the Cauchy argument at the end of Step 6 of the parent proof, stated for an arbitrary real sequence. The parent text reads: '(a_n) is a Cauchy sequence: otherwise there is ε > 0 such that for every i there are p(i), q(i) ≥ i with |a_{q(i)} − a_{p(i)}| ≥ ε; then p and q tend to ∞ while a_{q(i)} − a_{p(i)} does not tend to 0, contradicting the claim. Since ℝ is complete, (a_n) converges.' The parent applies it to a_n := X(η_n(ω)); the hypothesis is the claim of Step 6, which (CL) supplies for the reindexed approximations (G_{p(i)})_i and (G_{q(i)})_i.

1. (Cauchy criterion.) We show that a is a Cauchy sequence. By Metric.cauchySeq_iff, this means: for every ε > 0 there is N such that dist(a_i, a_j) = |a_i − a_j| < ε for all i, j ≥ N. Suppose not. Then there is ε > 0 such that for every N ∈ ℕ there are i, j ≥ N with |a_i − a_j| ≥ ε.
2. (Index maps.) By choice, pick for every N ∈ ℕ such indices p(N) ≥ N and q(N) ≥ N, so |a_{p(N)} − a_{q(N)}| ≥ ε. The identity map tends to ∞ and p(N) ≥ N, q(N) ≥ N for all N, so p and q tend to ∞ (tendsto_atTop_mono).
3. (Contradiction.) By the hypothesis applied to p and q, a(q(i)) − a(p(i)) → 0. By Metric.tendsto_nhds, eventually |a(q(i)) − a(p(i)) − 0| < ε; take one such i. Then |a_{p(i)} − a_{q(i)}| = |a_{q(i)} − a_{p(i)}| < ε. This contradicts |a_{p(i)} − a_{q(i)}| ≥ ε from step 2. Hence a is Cauchy.
4. (Completeness.) ℝ is complete, so the Cauchy sequence a converges to some s ∈ ℝ (cauchySeq_tendsto_of_complete). ∎
proof_key_steps: If a is not Cauchy, there are ε > 0 and, for every N, indices p(N), q(N) ≥ N with |a_{p(N)} − a_{q(N)}| ≥ ε.
Since p(N), q(N) ≥ N, both p and q tend to ∞, so the hypothesis gives a(q(i)) − a(p(i)) → 0, which contradicts the ε-gap at some i.
ℝ is complete, so the Cauchy sequence a converges.

subproblems.title: The support of a current characterized by compatible approximations G_n → G lies in closure(G(spt X)) (supplied Step 11)
subproblems.statement: Notation: ℝ^p := Eucl p; D_q(ℝ^p) := GeometricCurrentOn univ q and D^q(ℝ^p) := TestFormOn univ q; spt = support; for a covector γ and a continuous linear map T, γ∘T := γ.compContinuousLinearMap T. Let m, m′, k ∈ ℕ, X ∈ D_k(ℝ^m), S ∈ D_k(ℝ^{m′}) and G : ℝ^m → ℝ^{m′}, and let G_n : ℝ^m → ℝ^{m′} (n ∈ ℕ) be continuous maps with G_n → G uniformly on spt X. Assume that for every ω ∈ D^k(ℝ^{m′}) and every sequence (η_n) in D^k(ℝ^m) such that, for all sufficiently large n, there is an open N ⊆ ℝ^m with spt X ⊆ N and η_n(x) = ω(G_n(x))∘(fderiv ℝ G_n x) for all x ∈ N, the sequence X(η_n) converges to S(ω). Then spt S ⊆ closure(G(spt X)).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (m m' k : ℕ) (X : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Eucl m)) k) (S : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Eucl m')) k) (G : Eucl m → Eucl m') (Gj : ℕ → Eucl m → Eucl m'), (∀ n, Continuous (Gj n)) → TendstoUniformlyOn Gj G atTop X.support → (∀ (ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Eucl m')) k) (ηj : ℕ → TestFormOn (univ : Set (Eucl m)) k), (∀ᶠ n in atTop, ∃ N : Set (Eucl m), IsOpen N ∧ X.support ⊆ N ∧ ∀ x ∈ N, (ηj n : DifferentialForm (Eucl m) k) x = ((ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl m') k) (Gj n x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ (Gj n) x)) → Tendsto (fun n => X (ηj n)) atTop (𝓝 (S ω))) → S.support ⊆ closure (G '' X.support)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Step 11 of the parent proof. There the hypothesis is the characterization LipPF(X, G, S) of Step 9, applied to the reference sequence: the maps G_n are C^∞, hence continuous, and converge to G uniformly on (spt X)_{r/2} ⊇ spt X, hence on spt X. Recall the definitions. S vanishes on W (S.VanishesOn W) if S(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ D^k(ℝ^{m′}) with tsupport ω ⊆ W. zeroRegion(S) is the union of all open W ⊆ ℝ^{m′} with closure W compact, closure W ⊆ univ and S vanishing on W. spt S = univ ∖ zeroRegion(S).

1. (Setup.) Let y₀ ∈ spt S. Suppose, for contradiction, that y₀ ∉ closure(G(spt X)). The complement of the closed set closure(G(spt X)) is open and contains y₀, so there is ε > 0 with ball(y₀, ε) ∩ closure(G(spt X)) = ∅ (Metric.isOpen_iff). Put ρ := ε/3 > 0. For every x ∈ spt X, G(x) ∈ G(spt X) ⊆ closure(G(spt X)), so G(x) ∉ ball(y₀, ε), i.e. dist(G(x), y₀) ≥ ε.
2. (S vanishes on W := ball(y₀, ρ).) Let ω ∈ D^k(ℝ^{m′}) with tsupport ω ⊆ W.
   (a) By uniform convergence on spt X (Metric.tendstoUniformlyOn_iff), for all sufficiently large n: dist(G(x), G_n(x)) < ρ for every x ∈ spt X.
   (b) Fix such an n and put N_n := G_n⁻¹(ℝ^{m′} ∖ tsupport ω). It is open: it is the preimage, under the continuous map G_n, of the open complement of the closed set tsupport ω.
   (c) spt X ⊆ N_n. Let x ∈ spt X and suppose G_n(x) ∈ tsupport ω. Then G_n(x) ∈ W, i.e. dist(G_n(x), y₀) < ρ. By step 1 and the triangle inequality, ε ≤ dist(G(x), y₀) ≤ dist(G(x), G_n(x)) + dist(G_n(x), y₀) < ρ + ρ = 2ε/3 < ε, a contradiction. So G_n(x) ∉ tsupport ω, i.e. x ∈ N_n.
   (d) Let x ∈ N_n. Then G_n(x) ∉ tsupport ω, so ω(G_n(x)) = 0 (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport). Hence ω(G_n(x))∘(fderiv ℝ G_n x) = 0, since the pull-back of the zero covector is zero. This is the value at x of the zero form 0 ∈ D^k(ℝ^m).
   (e) By (a)–(d), for all sufficiently large n the constant sequence η_n := 0 satisfies the compatibility condition of the hypothesis for ω, with N := N_n. Hence X(0) → S(ω). But X is linear, so X(0) = 0 for every n, and the constant sequence 0 converges to 0. Limits in ℝ are unique (tendsto_nhds_unique), so S(ω) = 0.
   As ω was arbitrary, S vanishes on W.
3. (y₀ ∈ zeroRegion(S).) W = ball(y₀, ρ) is open. Its closure lies in closedBall(y₀, ρ) (closure_ball_subset_closedBall), which is compact because ℝ^{m′} is proper (isCompact_closedBall). So closure W is compact, as a closed subset of a compact set, and closure W ⊆ univ. With step 2, W belongs to the family whose union is zeroRegion(S). Since ρ > 0, y₀ ∈ W, hence y₀ ∈ zeroRegion(S).
4. (Conclusion.) spt S = univ ∖ zeroRegion(S), so y₀ ∉ spt S, which contradicts step 1. Hence every point of spt S lies in closure(G(spt X)), i.e. spt S ⊆ closure(G(spt X)). ∎
proof_key_steps: A point y₀ ∉ closure(G(spt X)) has a ball of radius ε = 3ρ disjoint from that closure, so dist(G(x), y₀) ≥ 3ρ for x ∈ spt X.

Let ω be supported in ball(y₀, ρ), and let n be large enough that dist(G, G_n) < ρ on spt X. Then G_n(x) ∉ tsupport ω on the open set N_n := G_n⁻¹(ℝ^{m′} ∖ tsupport ω) ⊇ spt X, so the zero form is compatible with (G_n, ω).
The hypothesis then gives X(0) = 0 → S(ω), so S(ω) = 0, and S vanishes on ball(y₀, ρ).
That ball is open with compact closure, so y₀ ∈ zeroRegion(S), i.e. y₀ ∉ spt S.
